title: Absent comparison groups leave both plasticity contrast signs possible in selected Allen slice strata
abstract: We tested whether matched wiring comparisons can fix a plasticity contrast across selected Allen cortical slice groups. In Synaptic Physiology r2.1, the final sample had 191 mouse and 90 human excitatory connections. Groups matched recording, ordered Cre labels, and layers. With equal donor weight and equal group weight within donors, groups with both reciprocal and one-way connections held 13.17% of mouse weight and 5.99% of human weight. We clipped response changes to [-1,1], fixed measured group means, and allowed each absent group mean to range freely within those limits. Sharp completion intervals for early changes were -0.819 to 0.918 in mouse and -0.972 to 0.909 in human. Late changes and the difference of stored late and early summaries also allowed both signs. All 54 clipping and selection variants allowed both signs. These are conditional completion bounds, not confidence intervals or causal effects. The target assumes meaningful hypothetical means for absent wiring groups. It does not cover missing edges, outcome error, or all cortical tissue. Original code, a proof, aggregate estimates, a figure, hashes, and retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are excluded.

display.caption: Sharp completion intervals at clipping limit 1. Points show the observed contrast in groups with both wiring types. These intervals are not confidence intervals.
